key_insight: Expanding Flow Maps (EFMs) extend flow-based generation to variable-sized outputs by coupling an explicit expand step with a transport step, so the model can grow and denoise the state in one learned map.
engineering_relevance: This enables controllable generation of variable-length sequences and variable-size graphs, making flow models practical for real systems where output dimension is not fixed in advance.
method: Define Expanding Generative Flows (EFlows) over distributions with increasing dimensionality.
Factor each EFM into an expand operator that adds conditional noise/coordinates and a transport map that advances the expanded state.
Recover standard fixed-dimension flows as the special case where expansion is the identity; extend the same idea to the discrete simplex for graphs and sequences.
evidence_signal: The abstract claims the framework works across both continuous and discrete modalities, including variable-size graph and variable-length sequence generation.
watch_item: Performance may depend on learning stable expand operators and discrete simplex mappings, which could be challenging to optimize and implement robustly.
